findings.title: set_away acknowledges an unparseable return_time and silently clears the stored return instant
findings.claim: A schema-valid heatpump_optimizer.set_away call whose return_time is a non-empty string that is not a datetime (6 of 6 cases) returns without raising, turns or keeps away on with no return instant, and in 3 of 3 cases wipes a previously stored return time; action-exceptions (Silver) requires a ServiceValidationError for incorrect input (D10-criteria Q2: the done row fails at this site).
findings.mechanism: SERVICE_SCHEMA_SET_AWAY admits return_time as cv.string; handle_set_away passes it to HeatPumpOptimizerCoordinator.async_set_away, which runs away._parse_return_time -> drift.stored_instant; datetime.fromisoformat raises ValueError, stored_instant returns None, and async_set_away stores iso=None (the clear value) instead of refusing. The sibling apply_manual_plan refuses the same shape (manual_plan_invalid_expires_at).

evidence.unit: calls acknowledged of 6 unparseable return_time strings (cleared_existing_return=3 of 3; control_accepted=1)
evidence.machine: macOS arm64 8-core (box B1, local), venv-ci Python 3.14.7
evidence.contention_note: box shared with other finder seats and this seat's coverage run; the count is contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb: away._parse_return_time wrapped to raise ServiceValidationError on a non-empty unparseable string (the fix shape)

findings.metric_definition: Of 6 schema-valid set_away calls with a non-empty non-datetime return_time, the number that return without a HomeAssistantError.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every service field a handler parses beyond its schema is either parsed successfully or refused with ServiceValidationError; no unparseable value is acknowledged and stored as the absent value.

null_control.note: a parseable ISO return_time is accepted and stored, so the count is about unparseable input only

reproduction_steps: The call succeeds; the away switch is on and the away_return datetime entity is unknown, so away has no end
findings.proposed_fix_scope: services.py handle_set_away (or SERVICE_SCHEMA_SET_AWAY): parse return_time before the write and raise ServiceValidationError with a translation key when a non-empty value does not parse, as apply_manual_plan does for expires_at; strings.json and translations gain the key.

findings.title: Two button presses report success when their action is refused or fails (sysid disabled, diagnosis worker down)
findings.claim: Pressing 'Run system identification' with the feature off (the default) arms nothing and returns without raising, and pressing 'Diagnose last interval' while the process worker is unavailable returns without raising while its background task raises ProcessWorkerUnavailable: 2 of 2 refused/failed presses are acknowledged, against action-exceptions (Silver), whose note extends the rule to platform actions; the compliant siblings (ForceOptimizationButton, the diagnose_interval service) raise under the same failure (2 of 2).
findings.mechanism: SystemIdentificationButton.async_press and DiagnoseIntervalButton.async_press hand their work to entity.off_the_action (an entry background task) and return at once, so no outcome can reach the caller. SysID.arm returns False with only an INFO log when system_identification_enabled is False (DEFAULT_SYSID_ENABLED=False) while the button stays available; the diagnosis failure surfaces only as an unretrieved task exception. button.py's PARALLEL_UPDATES is 0, so off_the_action's stated reason (a held parallel-updates slot, RC2) no longer applies on this platform, and ForceOptimizationButton already awaits and raises.

findings.title: Config flow stores 41 non-connection settings in ConfigEntry.data, all of them options-flow settings
findings.claim: Walking the setup wizard's 'Continue setup' path at the forms' own defaults creates an entry whose data holds 41 keys that are not asked on the two connection screens (comfort band, thermal model, hot water, weather sensitivity), every one of them also an options-flow field, and options={} -- against the config-flow (Bronze) subcheck 'Uses ConfigEntry.data and ConfigEntry.options correctly' (settings not needed for the connection belong in options); the null arm (Finish setup now) holds 0.
findings.mechanism: HeatPumpOptimizerConfigFlow._create_setup_entry passes the whole wizard dict self._data as async_create_entry(data=...), with no options=. Every reader then merges {**entry.data, **entry.options}, so a wizard value can be overridden by an option but never removed by one; const.py's two-zone comment records that consequence (zone keys the initial flow wrote into entry.data 'where options cannot erase them'), which needed CONF_TWO_ZONE_MODE as a workaround.

findings.title: two_zone_mode 'auto' forces two zones, so a single-zone install's options flow hides its whole-house heat loss
findings.claim: For an entry with no zone key, with two_zone_mode absent or 'auto' (2 of 2 single-zone entries), ThermalParameters.from_config reports two_zone_enabled=True and the options flow's thermal_model page does not render house_heat_loss_coefficient. The questionnaire also derives zone masses for a single-storey answer set. So the UI cannot configure the parameter the single-zone model reads, a config-flow (Bronze) failure (D10-criteria Q2). Null controls: two_zone_mode 'off' renders the field (1), and zone keys present hide it by design (1).
findings.mechanism: ThermalParameters.from_config tests `two_zone_mode in (const.TWO_ZONE_MODE_ON, const.DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE)`. DEFAULT_TWO_ZONE_MODE is 'auto', so 'auto' and every entry without the key take the forced-on branch, never the presence rule the function's own comment says 'auto' keeps. config_flow._single_zone, which gates the _OPTION_FIELDS row for house_heat_loss_coefficient (when=_single_zone), and presets.preset_from_config both read this predicate. The same predicate selects the model the solver runs; that consequence is outside this cell and is passed on as a lead.

findings.title: Flow tests never show recovery after 51 of 53 rendered errors (config, options, reconfigure)
findings.claim: Of the 53 distinct (flow, step, error) triples that tests/config_flow_steps.py makes the flows render, 51 never appear in a flow that later finishes, and 49 never appear in a flow that even moves past the erroring page. Reauthentication (2 of 2) is the only kind tested to recovery. config-flow-test-coverage (Bronze) requires that after each error 'the test fixes the cause and finishes the flow' for the user, reconfigure, reauthentication and options flows.
findings.mechanism: Each error branch is exercised on its own fresh flow (fresh_flow / fresh_options) that is dropped after the error assertion. Only the reauth test resubmits the same flow and finishes it (reauth_successful). So the row's done rests on statement coverage (config_flow_percent_floor 100.0) and does not show the recovery the rule asks for.

findings.title: test-coverage register row says done; on the round's tree 34 of 95 modules are below 95% (config_flow.py 99.21%)
findings.claim: Under every default-gate test script, each traced on its own and combined (fast + e2e + stress, 25 scripts), 34 of 95 modules are below the Silver rule's 95% statement coverage. The lowest are duty_legs.py 31.78, heat_curve.py 38.28, repairs.py 44.12, disinfection.py 47.66 and services.py 56.06; the package is at 91.38%. config_flow.py is at 99.21% (8 statements missed) against config-flow-test-coverage's 100%. quality_scale.yaml marks both rows done (D10-criteria Q2/Q3).
findings.mechanism: The register keys test-coverage to the recorded floors in tests/coverage_budgets.json (module_percent_floor 95.0, config_flow_percent_floor 100.0) rather than to a fresh measurement of the tree. On this tree 15 of the 25 measured scripts exit non-zero, tests/entities.py among them (it dies at import, see leads), and what a failing script leaves unexecuted is uncovered. Dropping entities alone moves only 34 -> 38 modules, so the shortfall is spread across the suite and not one crash.
